text:
incident-bot: Pager alert P1 — GPU OOM spikes on decode cluster r-decode-prod-3. Multiple container restarts observed. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/decode-oom>. Paging oncall.

alice (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Adding context channel and grabbing logs.

raj (sre): +1. Do we know customer impact yet? 5xx rate and any specific model? Metrics show a big jump starting ~2154321900.

kim (eng-runtime): Logs from node r-decode-prod-3-7:
```
[2154321895] E CUDA OOM: failed to allocate 1.2GB (out of 10.0GB)
[2154321895] E decode: stream loop exception: runtime_error: CUDA out of memory
[2154321896] I kubelet: container exited code=137, restarting
[2154321901] I request: id=abc123 client=acmelens model=redwood-XL-stream max_tokens=10000 streaming=true
```
Looks like one client request requested max_tokens=10000 and triggered runaway generation that exhausted the GPU KV cache. We're seeing repeated restarts (node flap) which makes the serving process drop in-flight streaming requests -> 503s.

jordan (product): That client is AcmeLens integration — they recently flipped an experimental parameter that allows them to suggest token budgets. They might be passing through their UI value unchecked.

lucy (cs): AcmeLens contacted support — experiencing chat truncations and ~40% request failures since 2154321900. Ticket #INC-6312 opened, pinged their SRE.

alice (oncall): Immediate mitigations I will apply now:
- Rate-limit incoming requests per-client to 10 RPS
- Enforce max_tokens hard cap at ingress = 2048
- Disable streaming for redwood-XL-stream temporarily (switch to non-streaming decode path)
- Route traffic from r-decode-prod-3 to r-decode-prod-5 fallback pool while we drain the node

kim (eng-runtime): Patch ready for ingress validator. Small snippet:
```
if request.max_tokens > 2048:
    request.max_tokens = 2048
    log.warn("capped max_tokens from %d to 2048", orig)
```
I'll push hotfix to edge route in a sec.

deploy-bot: Triggered deploy: edge/validate-max-tokens v2026.3-hotfix -> rolling to 6 pods. CI quick-tests passed. <https://ci.internal/build/5421>

alice (oncall): Applying temporary rate limit for client acmelens -> 5 RPS, global per-client cap 10 RPS. Also disabling streaming on model redwood-XL-stream via routing override.

raj (sre): Observability: 5xxs peaked at 11% at 2154321920. After rate-limit + cap + routing override, 5xxs down to 1.5% at 2154322050. Node r-decode-prod-3 still rebooting every ~30s, marking cordon->drain.

kim (eng-runtime): Confirmed the patch is live on edge. We see requests are being capped: log snippet:
```
[2154321960] I edge: capped request.max_tokens client=acmelens orig=10000 capped=2048
```
Also disabled streaming flags and forced fallback to non-streaming model version (redwood-XL-nostream-v2).

lucy (cs): Notifying AcmeLens: "We're aware of an issue causing increased errors and interruptions. We've applied mitigations (rate limits and token caps) — you'll see degraded throughput but fewer errors. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline." They acknowledged, asked for estimated timeline.

jordan (product): Can we confirm any regression windows? Need to know if responses changed quality because non-streaming path truncates earlier.

kim (eng-runtime): Quick eval on sample requests from AcmeLens: latency increased ~80ms, median tokens reduced due to cap. Quality delta small on standard prompts, but long-form generation may be truncated. We'll include that in customer note.

raj (sre): Current status: cluster r-decode-prod-3 cordoned + drained, pods rescheduled to r-decode-prod-5/r-decode-canary. Error rate stabilized. Still seeing OOM traces on old node before drain.

alice (oncall): Handoff incoming — setting summary for next oncall @lee (oncall-next):
- Incident: GPU OOM caused by runaway decode due to client-supplied max_tokens=10000 on Model redwood-XL-stream
- Impact: AcmeLens ~40% failures, global 5xx spike to 11%, some other clients saw transient drops
- Mitigations applied: per-client rate-limits, ingress max_tokens hard-cap 2048, streaming disabled on redwood-XL-stream, drained/cordoned node, traffic routed to fallback pool, hotfix deployed edge/validate-max-tokens
- Next actions: investigate why KV cache didn't protect against extreme seq lengths, review admission control for token budgets, postmortem + RCA, customer follow-up (cs owns)

lee (oncall-next): Ack. I'll take the follow-up. Will start digging into KV cache throttling logic and schedule postmortem. Please tag me on the RCA doc.

lucy (cs): Created customer follow-up email draft and shared ticket with timeline. Will coordinate SLA credits if needed.

kim (eng-runtime): Filing bug: INF-1209 "KV cache eviction doesn't bound memory under extreme max_tokens -> OOM" and PR for admission control INF-1210.

raj (sre): Monitoring note: keep the ingress cap for 24h and watch for any recurrences. If we see OOMs again, escalate to scale up GPU pool and enable emergency fallback to smaller quantized variants.

alice (oncall): Closing active page. Marking incident as mitigated. Leaving ingress cap and streaming-off as safe defaults until engineering PRs land. Will draft postmortem template. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated -> status: mitigated. Link to incident doc: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/2154321987>
